issues.legal_issue: The restriction on taking cognizance of certain document-related offences for want of a court complaint does not apply when only a copy of the allegedly forged document, and not the document itself, was produced in a court proceeding.
material_facts: A criminal prosecution alleged that a partnership deed had been forged and that offences involving the deed had been committed.
A copy of the deed was relied on in a civil proceeding to obtain a temporary injunction.
The original deed was not produced in the civil proceeding.
The magistrate declined to frame charges for certain offences without a complaint from the civil court, and the High Court directed that fresh charges be framed.
issues.conclusion: The statutory restriction did not apply because the allegedly forged document itself was not produced in court. The direction to frame fresh charges was confirmed on that ground, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 195(1)(b)(ii) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 bars cognizance of specified offences alleged in respect of a document produced or given in evidence in a court proceeding unless there is a complaint by that court. Production of a copy does not amount to production of the document itself, applying the plain grammatical meaning and practical sense of the provision. The Court relied on Sanmukhsingh v. The King, [1949] L.R. 77 I.A. 7, and Budhu Ram v. State of Rajasthan, [1963] 3 S.C.R. 376.

predicates.forgery_prosecution_related_to_court_pro: A criminal prosecution alleges an offence involving a document connected with a court proceeding.
predicates.only_copy_produced: A party produced or relied on a copy of the allegedly forged document in the court proceeding.
predicates.original_document_not_produced: The allegedly forged original document was not produced or given in evidence in the court proceeding.

issues.definition: When a document-forgery prosecution is connected with a court proceeding, only a copy was produced, and the original was not produced, the court may take cognizance without a complaint from that court.
